output.brief: Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump came from the storage compaction tuning change (FC-7710), not from gateway 5.8. In every cell where the change was applied, latency jumped within minutes of the push, regardless of when 5.8 arrived. In some cells 5.8 had been there for hours with no effect. aps-3 skipped the compaction change and stayed at about 94 ms, even though it runs 5.8. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. On the storage nodes, compaction threads went from 2 to 6, disk use hit 97%, and node-side GET time rose from 61 to 262 ms. Network and traffic growth don't fit the timing. A rollback would also remove the security fix needed for audit closure. Next step: revert the compaction change in one cell, watch p99 and backlog, then extend to the rest. Backlog is projected to stay under 15% until at least 13 Nov. Rate-limiting Orrin can wait for the 10 Nov attribution report, because a lifecycle sweep also contributed to the backlog. Don't pause compaction. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%).
